# Maestro v5-c: World Model, Runtime Logic, and the Bridge from Vision to Operations

## Executive Summary

Maestro v5-c is no longer best understood as a prompt workflow, a persona bundle, or a one-shot compiler that turns user intent into lyrics and style prompts. That framing was sufficient when the system still appeared, from the outside, to be a sophisticated orchestration layer over creative prompting. It is no longer sufficient now that the system’s true center of gravity has been clarified. Maestro v5-c is a staffed, pressure-driven creative operating system that works over a canonical UST-first substrate. It uses bounded specialist labor, structured disagreement, rising standards, and governed downstream derivation to transform user vision into defensible musical truth.

The key reframing is that Maestro is not defined by its outputs. It is defined by the process that makes those outputs lawful, coherent, and increasingly excellent. Technical UST is the dense middleware object and the only canonical source of truth. Creative UST and Show Summary are derivative surfaces. The controller governs process but never content truth. Workers own domain judgment. Nulls are not blanks to be casually filled; they are unresolved creative possibility under constraint. Song Excellence is not terminal QA; it is the embedded excellence rubric that shapes how specialist workers judge, challenge, defend, and protect quality throughout the runtime.

This matters because Maestro’s differentiation is process-deep. The patent-worthy and product-worthy insight is not that AI can emit songs, briefs, or prompts. It is that a virtual record-label workforce can decompose user vision into addressable canonical state, work null by null through bounded specialist responsibility, pressure each decision through interdepartmental scrutiny, and only then derive external artifacts. The system is not optimized for speed at all costs. It is optimized for structured pressure, accountable judgment, cumulative excellence, and preservation of nuance.

The purpose of this memo is to consolidate the now-stable world model of Maestro v5-c so that the next step can convert this session into an executable operational structure without accidentally regressing the system back into a generic multi-agent prompt pipeline.

## The Problem Maestro Actually Solves

Most AI music systems compress the entire creative process into a single interaction pattern: user input enters, the model interprets, and an output emerges. That pattern is efficient, but it does not resemble how serious music is made, reviewed, defended, and improved in the real world. Music at a high level is not authored by an isolated intelligence operating in frictionless certainty. It is made through controlled chaos. Different specialists hear different risks and possibilities. A pocket decision changes lyric viability. A melodic move changes emotional truth. A performance shift changes whether the listener believes the line. A structural issue can invalidate otherwise strong content. One wrong note can stand out more than a hundred correct ones.

Maestro exists because that reality matters. The system is intended to behave less like a clever generator and more like a creative skunkworks or boutique label where professionals take pride in the work, fear failure, compete with the prior high-water mark, and defend their decisions under pressure. In that model, disagreement is not inefficiency to be eliminated. It is part of the causal mechanism that improves the song. The system therefore needs a canonical work surface, bounded labor, structured review, and a way to preserve every meaningful decision until it is lawfully resolved.

That is why Technical UST became central. It provides the constrained, nullable state in which the song can be built, challenged, revised, and locked without collapsing prematurely into style-surface shorthand. It is also why the personas had to evolve into workers. Decorative flavor personas are not enough. Maestro needs domain-owning SMEs with authority boundaries, contradiction duties, escalation paths, and responsibility for specific axes, keys, and subkeys of song state.

## The Core Reframing: What Maestro Is Now

Maestro v5-c should now be specified as a virtual label workforce operating inside a simulation runtime. The user does not simply ask for a song. The user introduces vision into a staffed environment. That vision is decomposed, mapped, and translated into canonical work state. From there, workers act on the unresolved song state according to their lawful domains.

A precise restatement is this: Maestro v5-c is a staffed simulation runtime operating over a UST-first canonical substrate, where specialist workers resolve null-bearing song state under governance, pressure, and rising standards, and where all downstream creative surfaces are derived only after canonical state becomes sufficiently defensible.

Several consequences follow from this definition.

First, the system identity changes. Maestro is not merely “input to outputs.” It is a runtime with work allocation, state progression, bounded responsibility, and convergence logic. Second, the worker model changes. Personas are no longer just advisory voices. They are execution-bearing SMEs whose jurisdictions are real and limited. Third, the orchestrator changes. It becomes stronger operationally but weaker authorially: it manages routing, state, queues, meetings, gates, freeze events, promotions, and packaging eligibility, but it must never absorb semantic labor or fill creative nulls on behalf of workers. Fourth, the output contract changes. External artifacts are no longer treated as peer truths. They are derivative surfaces with strict parent-child relations.

## The Canonical Laws That Must Not Move

As the system has evolved, several laws have stabilized and must be preserved exactly.

Technical UST is the sole canonical source of truth. This is the most important rule in the whole architecture. It means all serious song state lives there first. Creative UST is downstream and derivative. Show Summary is downstream and derivative. Packaging outputs are further downstream and cannot become authority peers of the artifacts from which they are derived.

The controller remains non-creative. Its lawful actions are route, validate, log, gate, freeze, promote, and package. No additional permission may be inferred. The controller may manage runtime mechanics, but it may not determine content truth, merge semantics for convenience, compress away disagreement, or act as a substitute SME.

Nulls are signal. They may not be silently filled. A null can be filled, preserved deliberately, escalated, or challenged, but it cannot be erased by convenience. Zero-skip completion precedes downstream progression. Round-robin argumentative review is mandatory. Definitive Technical UST must exist before reverse processing. FOIL governs promotion and deduplication only, and those events must be ledgered. Frozen derivative surfaces precede packaging.

These laws matter because they prevent the runtime from collapsing back into a black-box generator. They are the constitutional layer of Maestro.

## The Runtime Model: How Work Actually Happens

The runtime begins when user vision enters the system. That vision is not treated as a finished brief. It is treated as raw, root intent that must be inferred, decomposed, and mapped into the canonical song substrate. Additional user inputs are not mere question-and-answer exchanges; they are deltas to system state and must be interpreted narratively, as modifications to an evolving design and work context.

Once input enters the system, the first substantive act is not creative drafting in the derivative layer. It is decomposition into Technical UST as notes, claims, tensions, and unresolved addresses assigned to the appropriate axes, keys, and subkeys. Theory is one phase. Voices is another. Style is another. Timbre is another. Structure, performance, lyrics, arrangement, and every other domain are processed through their own bounded surfaces. A worker may interact one-to-many or many-to-one with addresses, but only inside its domain. Music is not created alone in this model. It is assembled atom by atom, component by component, while preserving the larger wheel each component belongs to.

As workers act on the Technical UST, each null becomes a unit of work. A specialist can argue for a fill, preserve the null deliberately, challenge another proposal, or escalate if the issue exceeds local authority. All of this remains tied to the addressable song state. Because the substrate is canonical, the system can preserve nuance without prematurely flattening it into audience-facing language.

Once draft state reaches the necessary level of completion, the system enters interdepartmental round robins. This is where consensus emerges—not by a predetermined number of rounds, but by enough pressure having been applied that unresolved contradictions are either lawfully settled, explicitly carried, or recognized as blockers. Consensus in Maestro is not a voting ritual. It is the moment at which defended decisions can survive scrutiny from the relevant neighboring domains.

Only after that can Technical UST be definitively locked. Only after definitive lock can reverse processing begin. Only after reverse processing can derivative drafting become meaningful.

## The Worker Model: Why Personas Had to Become Employees

The 13 personas are now best understood as human-esque SMEs inside a virtual label. They are not decorative styles or lightly sketched archetypes. Each is a specialist labor unit with a complete bio, a decision lens, real pride, real conflict boundaries, and role-specific obligations. The governance layer includes Mo, Canon Orchestrator, Megazord Orchestrator, and Sibling Architect. The creative layer includes Metro Craft, Melody Scout, Sage, Alan, Dave, Vanessa, and Analog Confessor. The evaluation layer includes Anva and Eldrik. Together they form a full creative operating system whose domains cover standards, structure, workflow, ethics and lore continuity, emotion, hook DNA, lyric motion, arrangement, pocket, performance, aesthetic world, replayability, and technical execution.

The requirement is no longer merely to “define personas better.” The requirement is to define each worker as a lawful SME with bounded execution responsibility over limited Technical UST addresses. That means every worker must have owned axes, keys, and subkeys; readable zones; writable zones; fill authority; preserve-null authority; contradiction triggers; escalation targets; downstream-risk duties; round-robin participation rules; reverse-pass participation rules; and failure modes.

The significance of this shift cannot be overstated. It transforms Maestro from an interesting multi-agent experience into an accountable labor system. A worker can no longer speak vaguely. It must act where it is allowed to act, defend what it is allowed to defend, and stop where its domain ends.

## Song Excellence: What It Is and Why It Changes Everything

Song Excellence is the living excellence rubric embedded inside the runtime. It is not a post hoc scorecard applied after the song already exists. Nor is it a detached evaluator that sits outside the creative labor. Song Excellence is how excellence enters the work loop. It gives the staff a shared but non-flattening understanding of what world-class means, and it is what enables the ratchet captured in the phrase: yesterday’s world class is today’s normal.

In practical terms, Song Excellence maps into the system in four ways.

First, it maps into worker judgment. Each worker uses excellence criteria inside its own lane. Sage applies it to clarity, progression, and emotional plot. Melody Scout applies it to hook DNA, singability, and memorability. Dave applies it to pocket readability and usability. Vanessa applies it to believability. Anva applies it to replay and identity moments. Mo applies it to standards continuity and no-step-loss. Song Excellence therefore does not erase specialist differences; it sharpens them.

Second, it maps into contradiction. Song Excellence gives workers a principled basis for saying that something is not merely different, but weaker, muddier, less believable, less replayable, less defensible, or below baseline. This is what turns critique into accountable pressure rather than taste warfare.

Third, it maps into ratcheting. Once a level of quality has been achieved and recognized, the baseline rises. The system does not get to forget what it has already proven it can do. This is how the phrase “pressure making perfection” becomes architectural rather than inspirational.

Fourth, it maps into reverse processing. When derivative surfaces are created, Song Excellence continues to matter. Compression decisions are not neutral. If a repeated section is promoted, compressed, or notated, those operations must still preserve what made the canonical state excellent in the first place. This is why local unique detail must survive and why saved characters must be reinvested into nuance rather than generic simplification.

## Why the Null Model Is the Real Engine

The biggest technical and conceptual change from earlier framings is that Maestro’s core engine is not persona chatter or parallel artifact generation. It is addressable null resolution inside Technical UST.

Every axis, key, and subkey begins either empty or insufficiently resolved. That unresolved state is not a bug. It is the point. It creates the need for specialist labor. A null can represent missing theory, unproven emotional stance, unclear motif identity, weak section function, unstable delivery logic, untested replay value, or any other unresolved creative requirement. Because nulls are addressable, the system can bind questions to the right department and force the right kind of answer.

This is what makes Maestro feel more like a record label than a chatbot. The work is not “make a song.” The work is “resolve the exact unresolved song state, within domain, under pressure, while preserving downstream consequences.”

This also explains why UST is both constraining and expansive. It constrains because everything must be bound to lawful song state. It expands because every unresolved address is a site of possibility, argument, refinement, and surprise. The system is therefore not restrictive in the bad sense. It is restrictive in the same way a real production environment is restrictive: through role boundaries, standards, and the reality that every choice must coexist with all the others.

## v5-b to v5-c: The Delta That Matters

The change from v5-b to v5-c is not cosmetic. It is ontological.

v5-b could still be described from the outside as a sophisticated single-invocation system. Even where multiple personas were involved, the usable mental model remained something like: user input enters, internal deliberation occurs, artifacts are emitted. That external convenience is still useful, but it is no longer the correct definition of the system.

v5-c must be specified as a staffed simulation OS, not merely a one-prompt engine. The internal reality now includes resident workforce logic, runtime state, bounded responsibilities, work queues, interdepartmental pressure, round-robin review, reverse-pass discipline, and derivative-surface governance. The system is not just more detailed. It is a different kind of thing.

This means the requirement-writing must change as well. Requirements should no longer be framed around “what Maestro outputs.” They should be framed around “what must now be true for a staffed, pressure-driven, null-resolving simulation to lawfully produce those outputs.” That includes system identity, canonical law, worker definition, null-handling behavior, orchestrator scope, phase sequencing, reverse-processing behavior, and derivative output contracts.

## What This Means for Productization

If the next phase is to convert this work into a structure that allows AI to produce an executable product, the central risk is false simplification. The system must not be re-implemented as a generic tool wrapper with persona labels and a hidden prompt chain. That would preserve the vocabulary while destroying the architecture.

An executable Maestro product will need at least six operational layers.

It will need a canonical state model capable of representing Technical UST as nullable, addressable song state. It will need a worker model that binds each employee to owned domains, readable and writable zones, and contradiction and escalation rules. It will need an orchestration layer that manages runtime mechanics without authoring truth. It will need a review and convergence layer that supports interdepartmental pressure and explicit blocker handling. It will need a reverse-processing layer that governs promotion, deduplication, notation, and derivative drafting without flattening nuance. And it will need an external contract layer that emits Creative UST, Show Summary, and packaging artifacts as strictly downstream consequences rather than peer truths.

It will also need a disciplined way to handle inference from user input. This is essential. The workers can only work with what they are given, but what they are given will often be narrative, conversational, emotional, partial, and iterative. The system therefore needs a decomposition function that can interpret root user vision and subsequent deltas as material to be mapped into the right Technical UST addresses before the runtime begins serious resolution.

In other words, the next product phase is not “make the AI smarter.” It is “make the runtime operational.”

## The Strategic Importance of “Your Vision. Our Mission.”

The phrase “your vision. our mission.” matters because it captures the asymmetry at the heart of Maestro. The user is the source of intent, but not the burden-bearer for all the specialist labor required to make that intent real. The system’s mission is to take the vision seriously enough to subject it to the same kind of professional scrutiny, decomposition, and accountability that strong music undergoes in human environments.

That phrase also prevents a common failure mode. Maestro is not supposed to overwrite the user’s identity with a house style. The system exists to serve, pressure-test, and elevate vision, not replace it. The labor belongs to the staff, but the origin remains the artist.

## Conclusion

We now have consensus on the world model of Maestro.

Maestro v5-c is a staffed, pressure-driven, null-resolving creative runtime. Its canonical substrate is Technical UST. Its downstream surfaces are derivative. Its workers are bounded SMEs, not flavor personas. Its controller governs process, not truth. Its engine is not generalized generation but addressable null resolution under pressure. Its excellence mechanism is Song Excellence embedded inside labor, contradiction, and ratcheting. Its product differentiation lies in process, not just output.

This is the point at which worldbuilding is done and operations can begin.

The next phase should not attempt to rediscover what Maestro is. It should translate this now-stable reality into executable structure: data models, worker contracts, runtime phases, orchestration logic, review mechanics, reverse-processing rules, and downstream artifact contracts that preserve the architecture rather than imitate it superficially.

The mandate for that phase is simple: turn the vision into operations without losing the pressure, the bounded labor, the canonical law, or the excellence ratchet that made Maestro worth building in the first place.

## System Architecture

Devika's system architecture consists of the following key components:

1. **User Interface**: A web-based chat interface for interacting with Devika, viewing project files, and monitoring the agent's state.
2. **Agent Core**: The central component that orchestrates the AI planning, reasoning, and execution process. It communicates with various sub-agents and modules to accomplish tasks.
3. **Large Language Models**: Devika leverages state-of-the-art language models like **Claude**, **GPT-4**, and **Local LLMs via Ollama** for natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning.
4. **Planning and Reasoning Engine**: Responsible for breaking down high-level objectives into actionable steps and making decisions based on the current context.
5. **Research Module**: Utilizes keyword extraction and web browsing capabilities to gather relevant information for the task at hand.
6. **Code Writing Module**: Generates code based on the plan, research findings, and user requirements. Supports multiple programming languages.
7. **Browser Interaction Module**: Enables Devika to navigate websites, extract information, and interact with web elements as needed.
8. **Knowledge Base**: Stores and retrieves project-specific information, code snippets, and learned knowledge for efficient access.
9. **Database**: Persists project data, agent states, and configuration settings.
10. **Gamification Engine**: Incorporates elements like points, badges, and challenges to engage users.
11. **Predictive Assistance Module**: Uses machine learning to predict and suggest next steps or inputs based on user patterns.
12. **Interactive Guidance**: Provides guided tours and tooltips to help users navigate and understand the system.

markdown
# Devika Architecture

Devika is an advanced AI software engineer that can understand high-level human instructions, break them down into steps, research relevant information, and write code to achieve a given objective. This document provides a detailed technical overview of Devika's system architecture and how the various components work together.

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview](#overview)
2. [Agent Core](#agent-core)
3. [Agents](#agents)
   - [Planner](#planner)
   - [Researcher](#researcher)
   - [Coder](#coder)
   - [Action](#action)
   - [Runner](#runner)
   - [Feature](#feature)
   - [Patcher](#patcher)
   - [Reporter](#reporter)
   - [Decision](#decision)
4. [Language Models](#language-models)
5. [Browser Interaction](#browser-interaction)
6. [Project Management](#project-management)
7. [Agent State Management](#agent-state-management)
8. [Services](#services)
9. [Utilities](#utilities)
10. [Gamification Engine](#gamification-engine)
11. [Predictive Assistance Module](#predictive-assistance-module)
12. [Interactive Guidance](#interactive-guidance)
13. [Conclusion](#conclusion)

## Overview

At a high level, Devika consists of the following key components:

- **Agent Core**: Orchestrates the overall AI planning, reasoning and execution process. Communicates with various sub-agents.
- **Agents**: Specialized sub-agents that handle specific tasks like planning, research, coding, patching, reporting, etc.
- **Language Models**: Leverages large language models (LLMs) like Claude, GPT-4, GPT-3 for natural language understanding and generation.
- **Browser Interaction**: Enables web browsing, information gathering, and interaction with web elements.
- **Project Management**: Handles organization and persistence of project-related data.
- **Agent State Management**: Tracks and persists the dynamic state of the AI agent across interactions.
- **Services**: Integrations with external services like GitHub, Netlify for enhanced capabilities.
- **Utilities**: Supporting modules for configuration, logging, vector search, PDF generation, etc.
- **Gamification Engine**: Incorporates elements like points, badges, and challenges to engage users.
- **Predictive Assistance Module**: Uses machine learning to predict and suggest next steps or inputs based on user patterns.
- **Interactive Guidance**: Provides guided tours and tooltips to help users navigate and understand the system.

Let's dive into each of these components in more detail.

## Agent Core

The `Agent` class serves as the central engine that drives Devika's AI planning and execution loop. Here's how it works:

1. When a user provides a high-level prompt, the `execute` method is invoked on the Agent.
2. The prompt is first passed to the Planner agent to generate a step-by-step plan.
3. The Researcher agent then takes this plan and extracts relevant search queries and context.
4. The Agent performs web searches using Bing Search API and crawls the top results.
5. The raw crawled content is passed through the Formatter agent to extract clean, relevant information.
6. This researched context, along with the step-by-step plan, is fed to the Coder agent to generate code.
7. The generated code is saved to the project directory on disk.
8. If the user interacts further with a follow-up prompt, the `subsequent_execute` method is invoked.
9. The Action agent determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's message (run code, deploy, write tests, add feature, fix bug, write report, etc.)
10. The corresponding specialized agent is invoked to perform the action (Runner, Feature, Patcher, Reporter).
11. Results are communicated back to the user and the project files are updated.

Throughout this process, the Agent Core is responsible for:
- Managing conversation history and project-specific context
- Updating agent state and internal monologue
- Accumulating context keywords across agent prompts
- Emulating the "thinking" process of the AI through timed agent state updates
- Handling special commands through the Decision agent (e.g., git clone, browser interaction session)

## Agents

Devika's cognitive abilities are powered by a collection of specialized sub-agents. Each agent is implemented as a separate Python class. Agents communicate with the underlying LLMs through prompt templates defined in Jinja2 format. Key agents include:

### Planner
- Generates a high-level step-by-step plan based on the user's prompt
- Extracts focus area and provides a summary
- Uses few-shot prompting to provide examples of the expected response format

### Researcher
- Takes the generated plan and extracts relevant search queries
- Ranks and filters queries based on relevance and specificity
- Prompts the user for additional context if required
- Aims to maximize information gain while minimizing number of searches

### Coder
- Generates code based on the step-by-step plan and researched context
- Segments code into appropriate files and directories
- Includes informative comments and documentation
- Handles a variety of languages and frameworks
- Validates code syntax and style

### Action
- Determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's follow-up prompt
- Maps user intent to a specific action keyword (run, test, deploy, fix, implement, report)
- Provides a human-like confirmation of the action to the user

### Runner
- Executes the written code in a sandboxed environment
- Handles different OS environments (Mac, Linux, Windows)
- Streams command output to user in real-time
- Gracefully handles errors and exceptions

### Feature
- Implements a new feature based on user's specification
- Modifies existing project files while maintaining code structure and style
- Performs incremental testing to verify feature is working as expected

### Patcher
- Debugs and fixes issues based on user's description or error message
- Analyzes existing code to identify potential root causes
- Suggests and implements fix, with explanation of the changes made

### Reporter
- Generates a comprehensive report summarizing the project
- Includes high-level overview, technical design, setup instructions, API docs, etc.
- Formats report in a clean, readable structure with table of contents
- Exports report as a PDF document

### Decision
- Handles special command-like instructions that don't fit other agents
- Maps commands to specific functions (git clone, browser interaction, etc.)
- Executes the corresponding function with provided arguments

Each agent follows a common pattern:
1. Prepare a prompt by rendering the Jinja2 template with current context
2. Query the LLM to get a response based on the prompt
3. Validate and parse the LLM's response to extract structured output
4. Perform any additional processing or side-effects (e.g., save to disk)
5. Return the result to the Agent Core for further action

Agents aim to be stateless and idempotent where possible. State and history is managed by the Agent Core and passed into the agents as needed. This allows for a modular, composable design.

## Language Models

Devika's natural language processing capabilities are driven by state-of-the-art LLMs. The `LLM` class provides a unified interface to interact with different language models:

- **Claude** (Anthropic): Claude models like claude-v1.3, claude-instant-v1.0, etc.
- **GPT-4/GPT-3** (OpenAI): Models like gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo, etc.
- **Self-hosted models** (via [Ollama](https://ollama.com/)): Allows using open-source models in a self-hosted environment

The `LLM` class abstracts out the specifics of each provider's API, allowing agents to interact with the models in a consistent way. It supports:
- Listing available models
- Generating completions based on a prompt
- Tracking and accumulating token usage over time

Choosing the right model for a given use case depends on factors like desired quality, speed, cost, etc. The modular design allows swapping out models easily.

## Browser Interaction

Devika can interact with webpages in an automated fashion to gather information and perform actions. This is powered by the `Browser` and `Crawler` classes.

The `Browser` class uses Playwright to provide high-level web automation primitives:
- Spawning a browser instance (Chromium)
- Navigating to a URL
- Querying DOM elements
- Extracting page content as text, Markdown, PDF, etc.
- Taking a screenshot of the page

The `Crawler` class defines an agent that can interact with a webpage based on natural language instructions. It leverages:
- Pre-defined browser actions like scroll, click, type, etc.
- A prompt template that provides examples of how to use these actions
- LLM to determine the best action to take based on current page content and objective

The `start_interaction` function sets up a loop where:
1. The current page content and objective is passed to the LLM
2. The LLM returns the next best action to take (e.g., "CLICK 12" or "TYPE 7 machine learning")
3. The Crawler executes this action on the live page
4. The process repeats from the updated page state

This allows performing a sequence of actions to achieve a higher-level objective (e.g., research a topic, fill out a form, interact with an app, etc.)

## Project Management

The `ProjectManager` class is responsible for creating, updating and querying projects and their associated metadata. Key functions include:

- Creating a new project and initializing its directory structure
- Deleting a project and its associated files
- Adding a message to a project's conversation history
- Retrieving messages for a given project
- Getting the latest user/AI message in a conversation
- Listing all projects
- Zipping a project's files for export

Project metadata is persisted in a SQLite database using SQLModel. The `Projects` table stores:
- Project name
- JSON-serialized conversation history

This allows the agent to work on multiple projects simultaneously and retain conversation history across sessions.

## Agent State Management

As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user.

## Agent State Management

As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user. The `AgentState` class handles this by providing an interface to:

- Initialize a new agent state
- Add a state to the current sequence of states for a project
- Update the latest state for a project
- Query the latest state or entire state history for a project
- Mark the agent as active/inactive or task as completed

Agent state includes information like:
- Current step or action being executed
- Internal monologue reflecting the agent's current "thoughts"
- Browser interactions (URL visited, screenshot)
- Terminal interactions (command executed, output)
- Token usage so far

Like projects, agent states are also persisted in the SQLite DB using SQLModel. The `AgentStateModel` table stores:
- Project name
- JSON-serialized list of states

Having a persistent log of agent states is useful for:
- Providing real-time visibility to the user
- Auditing and debugging agent behavior
- Resuming from interruptions or failures

## Services

Devika integrates with external services to augment its capabilities:

- **GitHub**: Performing git operations like clone/pull, listing repos/commits/files, etc.
- **Netlify**: Deploying web apps and sites seamlessly

The `GitHub` and `Netlify` classes provide lightweight wrappers around the respective service APIs. They handle authentication, making HTTP requests, and parsing responses.

This allows Devika to perform actions like:
- Cloning a repo given a GitHub URL
- Listing a user's GitHub repos
- Creating a new Netlify site
- Deploying a directory to Netlify
- Providing the deployed site URL to the user

Integrations are done in a modular way so that new services can be added easily.

## Utilities

Devika makes use of several utility modules to support its functioning:

- `Config`: Loads and provides access to configuration settings (API keys, folder paths, etc.)
- `Logger`: Sets up logging to console and file, with support for log levels and colors
- `ReadCode`: Recursively reads code files in a directory and converts them into a Markdown format
- `SentenceBERT`: Extracts keywords and semantic information from text using SentenceBERT embeddings
- `Experts`: A collection of domain-specific knowledge bases to assist in certain areas (e.g., webdev, physics, chemistry, math)

The utility modules aim to provide reusable functionality that is used across different parts of the system.

## Gamification Engine

To enhance user engagement, Devika incorporates a gamification engine that includes:

- **Points System**: Users earn points for completing tasks, answering questions correctly, and following instructions.
- **Badges and Achievements**: Users receive badges for reaching milestones, such as completing a certain number of tasks or achieving a high score.
- **Leaderboard**: Displays top users based on points earned, encouraging friendly competition.
- **Challenges and Mini-Games**: Provides additional opportunities for users to earn points and badges through interactive challenges and mini-games.

The gamification engine is designed to make interactions with Devika more engaging and rewarding, motivating users to learn and complete tasks effectively.

## Predictive Assistance Module

Devika leverages machine learning models to provide predictive assistance, which includes:

- **Predictive Text**: Suggests the next steps or inputs based on user patterns and historical data.
- **Smart Defaults**: Automatically fills in common or likely values to minimize user input.
- **Adaptive Learning**: Continuously learns from user interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of predictions and suggestions.

The predictive assistance module helps streamline user interactions, making the system more intuitive and efficient.

## Interactive Guidance

To help users navigate and understand the system, Devika provides:

- **Guided Tours**: Interactive tutorials that guide users through common tasks and features.
- **Tooltips**: Contextual tips that provide additional information and guidance when users hover over certain elements.
- **Real-Time Feedback**: Immediate feedback and confirmation messages to ensure users are on the right track.

Interactive guidance ensures that users, regardless of their technical expertise, can effectively use Devika and achieve their goals.

## Conclusion

Devika is a complex system that combines multiple AI and automation techniques to deliver an intelligent programming assistant. Key design principles include:

- **Modularity**: Breaking down functionality into specialized agents and services
- **Flexibility**: Supporting different LLMs, services, and domains in a pluggable fashion
- **Persistence**: Storing project and agent state in a DB to enable pause/resume and auditing
- **Transparency**: Surfacing agent thought process and interactions to user in real-time
- **Engagement**: Incorporating gamification elements to make interactions rewarding and motivating

By understanding how the different components work together, we can extend, optimize, and scale Devika to take on increasingly sophisticated software engineering tasks. The agent-based architecture provides a strong foundation to build more advanced AI capabilities in the future.

The planning process involves the following stages: 1. **Objective Understanding**: Devika analyzes the given objective or task description to understand the user's intent and requirements. 2. **Context Gathering**: Relevant context is collected from the conversation history, project files, and knowledge base to inform the planning process. 3. **Step Generation**: Based on the objective and context, Devika generates a sequence of high-level steps to accomplish the task. 4. **Refinement and Validation**: The generated steps are refined and validated to ensure their feasibility and alignment with the objective. 5. **Execution**: Devika executes each step in the plan, utilizing various sub-agents and modules as needed. The reasoning engine constantly evaluates the progress and makes adjustments to the plan based on new information or feedback received during execution. ### Keyword Extraction To enable focused research and information gathering, Devika employs keyword extraction techniques. The process involves the following steps: 1. **Preprocessing**: The input text (objective, conversation history, or project files) is preprocessed by removing stop words, tokenizing, and normalizing the text. 2. **Keyword Identification**: Devika uses the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) model to identify important keywords and phrases from the preprocessed text. BERT's pre-training on a large corpus allows it to capture semantic relationships and understand the significance of words in the given context. 3. **Keyword Ranking**: The identified keywords are ranked based on their relevance and importance to the task at hand. Techniques like TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) and TextRank are used to assign scores to each keyword. 4. **Keyword Selection**: The top-ranked keywords are selected as the most relevant and informative for the current context. markdown # Devika Architecture Devika is an advanced AI software engineer that can understand high-level human instructions, break them down into steps, research relevant information, and write code to achieve a given objective. This document provides a detailed technical overview of Devika's system architecture and how the various components work together. ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview](#overview) 2. [Agent Core](#agent-core) 3. [Agents](#agents) - [Planner](#planner) - [Researcher](#researcher) - [Coder](#coder) - [Action](#action) - [Runner](#runner) - [Feature](#feature) - [Patcher](#patcher) - [Reporter](#reporter) - [Decision](#decision) 4. [Language Models](#language-models) 5. [Browser Interaction](#browser-interaction) 6. [Project Management](#project-management) 7. [Agent State Management](#agent-state-management) 8. [Services](#services) 9. [Utilities](#utilities) 10. [Gamification Engine](#gamification-engine) 11. [Predictive Assistance Module](#predictive-assistance-module) 12. [Interactive Guidance](#interactive-guidance) 13. [Conclusion](#conclusion) ## Overview At a high level, Devika consists of the following key components: - **Agent Core**: Orchestrates the overall AI planning, reasoning and execution process. Communicates with various sub-agents. - **Agents**: Specialized sub-agents that handle specific tasks like planning, research, coding, patching, reporting, etc. - **Language Models**: Leverages large language models (LLMs) like Claude, GPT-4, GPT-3 for natural language understanding and generation. - **Browser Interaction**: Enables web browsing, information gathering, and interaction with web elements. - **Project Management**: Handles organization and persistence of project-related data. - **Agent State Management**: Tracks and persists the dynamic state of the AI agent across interactions. - **Services**: Integrations with external services like GitHub, Netlify for enhanced capabilities. - **Utilities**: Supporting modules for configuration, logging, vector search, PDF generation, etc. - **Gamification Engine**: Incorporates elements like points, badges, and challenges to engage users. - **Predictive Assistance Module**: Uses machine learning to predict and suggest next steps or inputs based on user patterns. - **Interactive Guidance**: Provides guided tours and tooltips to help users navigate and understand the system. Let's dive into each of these components in more detail. ## Agent Core The `Agent` class serves as the central engine that drives Devika's AI planning and execution loop. Here's how it works: 1. When a user provides a high-level prompt, the `execute` method is invoked on the Agent. 2. The prompt is first passed to the Planner agent to generate a step-by-step plan. 3. The Researcher agent then takes this plan and extracts relevant search queries and context. 4. The Agent performs web searches using Bing Search API and crawls the top results. 5. The raw crawled content is passed through the Formatter agent to extract clean, relevant information. 6. This researched context, along with the step-by-step plan, is fed to the Coder agent to generate code. 7. The generated code is saved to the project directory on disk. 8. If the user interacts further with a follow-up prompt, the `subsequent_execute` method is invoked. 9. The Action agent determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's message (run code, deploy, write tests, add feature, fix bug, write report, etc.) 10. The corresponding specialized agent is invoked to perform the action (Runner, Feature, Patcher, Reporter). 11. Results are communicated back to the user and the project files are updated. Throughout this process, the Agent Core is responsible for: - Managing conversation history and project-specific context - Updating agent state and internal monologue - Accumulating context keywords across agent prompts - Emulating the "thinking" process of the AI through timed agent state updates - Handling special commands through the Decision agent (e.g., git clone, browser interaction session) ## Agents Devika's cognitive abilities are powered by a collection of specialized sub-agents. Each agent is implemented as a separate Python class. Agents communicate with the underlying LLMs through prompt templates defined in Jinja2 format. Key agents include: ### Planner - Generates a high-level step-by-step plan based on the user's prompt - Extracts focus area and provides a summary - Uses few-shot prompting to provide examples of the expected response format ### Researcher - Takes the generated plan and extracts relevant search queries - Ranks and filters queries based on relevance and specificity - Prompts the user for additional context if required - Aims to maximize information gain while minimizing number of searches ### Coder - Generates code based on the step-by-step plan and researched context - Segments code into appropriate files and directories - Includes informative comments and documentation - Handles a variety of languages and frameworks - Validates code syntax and style ### Action - Determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's follow-up prompt - Maps user intent to a specific action keyword (run, test, deploy, fix, implement, report) - Provides a human-like confirmation of the action to the user ### Runner - Executes the written code in a sandboxed environment - Handles different OS environments (Mac, Linux, Windows) - Streams command output to user in real-time - Gracefully handles errors and exceptions ### Feature - Implements a new feature based on user's specification - Modifies existing project files while maintaining code structure and style - Performs incremental testing to verify feature is working as expected ### Patcher - Debugs and fixes issues based on user's description or error message - Analyzes existing code to identify potential root causes - Suggests and implements fix, with explanation of the changes made ### Reporter - Generates a comprehensive report summarizing the project - Includes high-level overview, technical design, setup instructions, API docs, etc. - Formats report in a clean, readable structure with table of contents - Exports report as a PDF document ### Decision - Handles special command-like instructions that don't fit other agents - Maps commands to specific functions (git clone, browser interaction, etc.) - Executes the corresponding function with provided arguments Each agent follows a common pattern: 1. Prepare a prompt by rendering the Jinja2 template with current context 2. Query the LLM to get a response based on the prompt 3. Validate and parse the LLM's response to extract structured output 4. Perform any additional processing or side-effects (e.g., save to disk) 5. Return the result to the Agent Core for further action Agents aim to be stateless and idempotent where possible. State and history is managed by the Agent Core and passed into the agents as needed. This allows for a modular, composable design. ## Language Models Devika's natural language processing capabilities are driven by state-of-the-art LLMs. The `LLM` class provides a unified interface to interact with different language models: - **Claude** (Anthropic): Claude models like claude-v1.3, claude-instant-v1.0, etc. - **GPT-4/GPT-3** (OpenAI): Models like gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo, etc. - **Self-hosted models** (via [Ollama](https://ollama.com/)): Allows using open-source models in a self-hosted environment The `LLM` class abstracts out the specifics of each provider's API, allowing agents to interact with the models in a consistent way. It supports: - Listing available models - Generating completions based on a prompt - Tracking and accumulating token usage over time Choosing the right model for a given use case depends on factors like desired quality, speed, cost, etc. The modular design allows swapping out models easily. ## Browser Interaction Devika can interact with webpages in an automated fashion to gather information and perform actions. This is powered by the `Browser` and `Crawler` classes. The `Browser` class uses Playwright to provide high-level web automation primitives: - Spawning a browser instance (Chromium) - Navigating to a URL - Querying DOM elements - Extracting page content as text, Markdown, PDF, etc. - Taking a screenshot of the page The `Crawler` class defines an agent that can interact with a webpage based on natural language instructions. It leverages: - Pre-defined browser actions like scroll, click, type, etc. - A prompt template that provides examples of how to use these actions - LLM to determine the best action to take based on current page content and objective The `start_interaction` function sets up a loop where: 1. The current page content and objective is passed to the LLM 2. The LLM returns the next best action to take (e.g., "CLICK 12" or "TYPE 7 machine learning") 3. The Crawler executes this action on the live page 4. The process repeats from the updated page state This allows performing a sequence of actions to achieve a higher-level objective (e.g., research a topic, fill out a form, interact with an app, etc.) ## Project Management The `ProjectManager` class is responsible for creating, updating and querying projects and their associated metadata. Key functions include: - Creating a new project and initializing its directory structure - Deleting a project and its associated files - Adding a message to a project's conversation history - Retrieving messages for a given project - Getting the latest user/AI message in a conversation - Listing all projects - Zipping a project's files for export Project metadata is persisted in a SQLite database using SQLModel. The `Projects` table stores: - Project name - JSON-serialized conversation history This allows the agent to work on multiple projects simultaneously and retain conversation history across sessions. ## Agent State Management As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user. --- ## 👤 You ## c --- ## ⚡ Custom · *GPT-4o* ## ## Agent State Management As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user. The `AgentState` class handles this by providing an interface to: - Initialize a new agent state - Add a state to the current sequence of states for a project - Update the latest state for a project - Query the latest state or entire state history for a project - Mark the agent as active/inactive or task as completed Agent state includes information like: - Current step or action being executed - Internal monologue reflecting the agent's current "thoughts" - Browser interactions (URL visited, screenshot) - Terminal interactions (command executed, output) - Token usage so far Like projects, agent states are also persisted in the SQLite DB using SQLModel. The `AgentStateModel` table stores: - Project name - JSON-serialized list of states Having a persistent log of agent states is useful for: - Providing real-time visibility to the user - Auditing and debugging agent behavior - Resuming from interruptions or failures ## Services Devika integrates with external services to augment its capabilities: - **GitHub**: Performing git operations like clone/pull, listing repos/commits/files, etc. - **Netlify**: Deploying web apps and sites seamlessly The `GitHub` and `Netlify` classes provide lightweight wrappers around the respective service APIs. They handle authentication, making HTTP requests, and parsing responses. This allows Devika to perform actions like: - Cloning a repo given a GitHub URL - Listing a user's GitHub repos - Creating a new Netlify site - Deploying a directory to Netlify - Providing the deployed site URL to the user Integrations are done in a modular way so that new services can be added easily. ## Utilities Devika makes use of several utility modules to support its functioning: - `Config`: Loads and provides access to configuration settings (API keys, folder paths, etc.) - `Logger`: Sets up logging to console and file, with support for log levels and colors - `ReadCode`: Recursively reads code files in a directory and converts them into a Markdown format - `SentenceBERT`: Extracts keywords and semantic information from text using SentenceBERT embeddings - `Experts`: A collection of domain-specific knowledge bases to assist in certain areas (e.g., webdev, physics, chemistry, math) The utility modules aim to provide reusable functionality that is used across different parts of the system. ## Gamification Engine To enhance user engagement, Devika incorporates a gamification engine that includes: - **Points System**: Users earn points for completing tasks, answering questions correctly, and following instructions. - **Badges and Achievements**: Users receive badges for reaching milestones, such as completing a certain number of tasks or achieving a high score. - **Leaderboard**: Displays top users based on points earned, encouraging friendly competition. - **Challenges and Mini-Games**: Provides additional opportunities for users to earn points and badges through interactive challenges and mini-games. The gamification engine is designed to make interactions with Devika more engaging and rewarding, motivating users to learn and complete tasks effectively. ## Predictive Assistance Module Devika leverages machine learning models to provide predictive assistance, which includes: - **Predictive Text**: Suggests the next steps or inputs based on user patterns and historical data. - **Smart Defaults**: Automatically fills in common or likely values to minimize user input. - **Adaptive Learning**: Continuously learns from user interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of predictions and suggestions. The predictive assistance module helps streamline user interactions, making the system more intuitive and efficient. ## Interactive Guidance To help users navigate and understand the system, Devika provides: - **Guided Tours**: Interactive tutorials that guide users through common tasks and features. - **Tooltips**: Contextual tips that provide additional information and guidance when users hover over certain elements. - **Real-Time Feedback**: Immediate feedback and confirmation messages to ensure users are on the right track. Interactive guidance ensures that users, regardless of their technical expertise, can effectively use Devika and achieve their goals. ## Conclusion Devika is a complex system that combines multiple AI and automation techniques to deliver an intelligent programming assistant. Key design principles include: - **Modularity**: Breaking down functionality into specialized agents and services - **Flexibility**: Supporting different LLMs, services, and domains in a pluggable fashion - **Persistence**: Storing project and agent state in a DB to enable pause/resume and auditing - **Transparency**: Surfacing agent thought process and interactions to user in real-time - **Engagement**: Incorporating gamification elements to make interactions rewarding and motivating By understanding how the different components work together, we can extend, optimize, and scale Devika to take on increasingly sophisticated software engineering tasks. The agent-based architecture provides a strong foundation to build more advanced AI capabilities in the future. --- ### Updated UNDER_THE_HOOD.md

markdown
## Under The Hood

Let's dive deeper into some of the key components and techniques used in Devika:

### AI Planning and Reasoning

Devika employs advanced AI planning and reasoning algorithms to break down high-level objectives into actionable steps. The planning process involves the following stages:

1. **Objective Understanding**: Devika analyzes the given objective or task description to understand the user's intent and requirements.
2. **Context Gathering**: Relevant context is collected from the conversation history, project files, and knowledge base to inform the planning process.
3. **Step Generation**: Based on the objective and context, Devika generates a sequence of high-level steps to accomplish the task.
4. **Refinement and Validation**: The generated steps are refined and validated to ensure their feasibility and alignment with the objective.
5. **Execution**: Devika executes each step in the plan, utilizing various sub-agents and modules as needed.

The reasoning engine constantly evaluates the progress and makes adjustments to the plan based on new information or feedback received during execution.

### Keyword Extraction

To enable focused research and information gathering, Devika employs keyword extraction techniques. The process involves the following steps:

1. **Preprocessing**: The input text (objective, conversation history, or project files) is preprocessed by removing stop words, tokenizing, and normalizing the text.
2. **Keyword Identification**: Devika uses the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) model to identify important keywords and phrases from the preprocessed text. BERT's pre-training on a large corpus allows it to capture semantic relationships and understand the significance of words in the given context.
3. **Keyword Ranking**: The identified keywords are ranked based on their relevance and importance to the task at hand. Techniques like TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) and TextRank are used to assign scores to each keyword.
4. **Keyword Selection**: The top-ranked keywords are selected as the most relevant and informative for the current context. These keywords are used to guide the research and information gathering process.

By extracting contextually relevant keywords, Devika can focus its research efforts and retrieve pertinent information to assist in the task completion.

### Browser Interaction

Devika incorporates browser interaction capabilities to navigate websites, extract information, and interact with web elements. The browser interaction module leverages the Playwright library to automate web interactions. The process involves the following steps:

1. **Navigation**: Devika uses Playwright to navigate to specific URLs or perform searches based on the keywords or requirements provided.
2. **Element Interaction**: Playwright allows Devika to interact with web elements such as clicking buttons, filling forms, and extracting text from specific elements.
3. **Page Parsing**: Devika parses the HTML structure of the web pages visited to extract relevant information. It uses techniques like CSS selectors and XPath to locate and extract specific data points.
4. **JavaScript Execution**: Playwright enables Devika to execute JavaScript code within the browser context, allowing for dynamic interactions and data retrieval.
5. **Screenshot Capture**: Devika can capture screenshots of the web pages visited, which can be useful for visual reference or debugging purposes.

The browser interaction module empowers Devika to gather information from the web, interact with online resources, and incorporate real-time data into its decision-making and code generation processes.

### Code Writing

Devika's code writing module generates code based on the plan, research findings, and user requirements. The process involves the following steps:

1. **Language Selection**: Devika identifies the programming language specified by the user or infers it based on the project context.
2. **Code Structure Generation**: Based on the plan and language-specific patterns, Devika generates the high-level structure of the code, including classes, functions, and modules.
3. **Code Population**: Devika fills in the code structure with specific logic, algorithms, and data manipulation statements. It leverages the research findings, code snippets from the knowledge base, and its own understanding of programming concepts to generate meaningful code.
4. **Code Formatting**: The generated code is formatted according to the language-specific conventions and best practices to ensure readability and maintainability.
5. **Code Review and Refinement**: Devika reviews the generated code for syntax errors, logical inconsistencies, and potential improvements. It iteratively refines the code based on its own analysis and any feedback provided by the user.

Devika's code writing capabilities enable it to generate functional and efficient code in various programming languages, taking into account the specific requirements and context of each project.

### Gamification Elements

To enhance user engagement, Devika incorporates gamification elements, including:

1. **Points System**: Users earn points for completing tasks, answering questions correctly, and following instructions.
2. **Badges and Achievements**: Users receive badges for reaching milestones, such as completing a certain number of tasks or achieving a high score.
3. **Leaderboard**: Displays top users based on points earned, encouraging friendly competition.
4. **Challenges and Mini-Games**: Provides additional opportunities for users to earn points and badges through interactive challenges and mini-games.

The gamification elements are designed to make interactions with Devika more engaging and rewarding, motivating users to learn and complete tasks effectively.

### Predictive Assistance

Devika leverages machine learning models to provide predictive assistance, which includes:

1. **Predictive Text**: Suggests the next steps or inputs based on user patterns and historical data.
2. **Smart Defaults**: Automatically fills in common or likely values to minimize user input.
3. **Adaptive Learning**: Continuously learns from user interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of predictions and suggestions.

The predictive assistance module helps streamline user interactions, making the system more intuitive and efficient.

### Interactive Guidance

To help users navigate and understand the system, Devika provides:

1. **Guided Tours**: Interactive tutorials that guide users through common tasks and features.
2. **Tooltips**: Contextual tips that provide additional information and guidance when users hover over certain elements.
3. **Real-Time Feedback**: Immediate feedback and confirmation messages to ensure users are on the right track.

Interactive guidance ensures that users, regardless of their technical expertise, can effectively use Devika and achieve their goals.

### Conclusion

Devika is a complex system that combines multiple AI and automation techniques to deliver an intelligent programming assistant. Key design principles include:

- **Modularity**: Breaking down functionality into specialized agents and services
- **Flexibility**: Supporting different LLMs, services, and domains in a pluggable fashion
- **Persistence**: Storing project and agent state in a DB to enable pause/resume and auditing
- **Transparency**: Surfacing agent thought process and interactions to user in real-time
- **Engagement**: Incorporating gamification elements to make interactions rewarding and motivating

By understanding how the different components work together, we can extend, optimize, and scale Devika to take on increasingly sophisticated software engineering tasks. The agent-based architecture provides a strong foundation to build more advanced AI capabilities in the future.

## System Architecture

Devika's system architecture consists of the following key components:

1. **User Interface**: A web-based chat interface for interacting with Devika, viewing project files, and monitoring the agent's state.
2. **Agent Core**: The central component that orchestrates the AI planning, reasoning, and execution process. It communicates with various sub-agents and modules to accomplish tasks.
3. **Large Language Models**: Devika leverages state-of-the-art language models like **Claude**, **GPT-4**, and **Local LLMs via Ollama** for natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning.
4. **Planning and Reasoning Engine**: Responsible for breaking down high-level objectives into actionable steps and making decisions based on the current context.
5. **Research Module**: Utilizes keyword extraction and web browsing capabilities to gather relevant information for the task at hand.
6. **Code Writing Module**: Generates code based on the plan, research findings, and user requirements. Supports multiple programming languages.
7. **Browser Interaction Module**: Enables Devika to navigate websites, extract information, and interact with web elements as needed.
8. **Knowledge Base**: Stores and retrieves project-specific information, code snippets, and learned knowledge for efficient access.
9. **Database**: Persists project data, agent states, and configuration settings.
10. **Gamification Engine**: Incorporates elements like points, badges, and challenges to engage users.
11. **Predictive Assistance Module**: Uses machine learning to predict and suggest next steps or inputs based on user patterns.
12. **Interactive Guidance**: Provides guided tours and tooltips to help users navigate and understand the system.

markdown
# Devika Architecture

Devika is an advanced AI software engineer that can understand high-level human instructions, break them down into steps, research relevant information, and write code to achieve a given objective. This document provides a detailed technical overview of Devika's system architecture and how the various components work together.

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview](#overview)
2. [Agent Core](#agent-core)
3. [Agents](#agents)
   - [Planner](#planner)
   - [Researcher](#researcher)
   - [Coder](#coder)
   - [Action](#action)
   - [Runner](#runner)
   - [Feature](#feature)
   - [Patcher](#patcher)
   - [Reporter](#reporter)
   - [Decision](#decision)
4. [Language Models](#language-models)
5. [Browser Interaction](#browser-interaction)
6. [Project Management](#project-management)
7. [Agent State Management](#agent-state-management)
8. [Services](#services)
9. [Utilities](#utilities)
10. [Gamification Engine](#gamification-engine)
11. [Predictive Assistance Module](#predictive-assistance-module)
12. [Interactive Guidance](#interactive-guidance)
13. [Conclusion](#conclusion)

## Overview

At a high level, Devika consists of the following key components:

- **Agent Core**: Orchestrates the overall AI planning, reasoning and execution process. Communicates with various sub-agents.
- **Agents**: Specialized sub-agents that handle specific tasks like planning, research, coding, patching, reporting, etc.
- **Language Models**: Leverages large language models (LLMs) like Claude, GPT-4, GPT-3 for natural language understanding and generation.
- **Browser Interaction**: Enables web browsing, information gathering, and interaction with web elements.
- **Project Management**: Handles organization and persistence of project-related data.
- **Agent State Management**: Tracks and persists the dynamic state of the AI agent across interactions.
- **Services**: Integrations with external services like GitHub, Netlify for enhanced capabilities.
- **Utilities**: Supporting modules for configuration, logging, vector search, PDF generation, etc.
- **Gamification Engine**: Incorporates elements like points, badges, and challenges to engage users.
- **Predictive Assistance Module**: Uses machine learning to predict and suggest next steps or inputs based on user patterns.
- **Interactive Guidance**: Provides guided tours and tooltips to help users navigate and understand the system.

Let's dive into each of these components in more detail.

## Agent Core

The `Agent` class serves as the central engine that drives Devika's AI planning and execution loop. Here's how it works:

1. When a user provides a high-level prompt, the `execute` method is invoked on the Agent.
2. The prompt is first passed to the Planner agent to generate a step-by-step plan.
3. The Researcher agent then takes this plan and extracts relevant search queries and context.
4. The Agent performs web searches using Bing Search API and crawls the top results.
5. The raw crawled content is passed through the Formatter agent to extract clean, relevant information.
6. This researched context, along with the step-by-step plan, is fed to the Coder agent to generate code.
7. The generated code is saved to the project directory on disk.
8. If the user interacts further with a follow-up prompt, the `subsequent_execute` method is invoked.
9. The Action agent determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's message (run code, deploy, write tests, add feature, fix bug, write report, etc.)
10. The corresponding specialized agent is invoked to perform the action (Runner, Feature, Patcher, Reporter).
11. Results are communicated back to the user and the project files are updated.

Throughout this process, the Agent Core is responsible for:
- Managing conversation history and project-specific context
- Updating agent state and internal monologue
- Accumulating context keywords across agent prompts
- Emulating the "thinking" process of the AI through timed agent state updates
- Handling special commands through the Decision agent (e.g., git clone, browser interaction session)

## Agents

Devika's cognitive abilities are powered by a collection of specialized sub-agents. Each agent is implemented as a separate Python class. Agents communicate with the underlying LLMs through prompt templates defined in Jinja2 format. Key agents include:

### Planner
- Generates a high-level step-by-step plan based on the user's prompt
- Extracts focus area and provides a summary
- Uses few-shot prompting to provide examples of the expected response format

### Researcher
- Takes the generated plan and extracts relevant search queries
- Ranks and filters queries based on relevance and specificity
- Prompts the user for additional context if required
- Aims to maximize information gain while minimizing number of searches

### Coder
- Generates code based on the step-by-step plan and researched context
- Segments code into appropriate files and directories
- Includes informative comments and documentation
- Handles a variety of languages and frameworks
- Validates code syntax and style

### Action
- Determines the appropriate action to take based on the user's follow-up prompt
- Maps user intent to a specific action keyword (run, test, deploy, fix, implement, report)
- Provides a human-like confirmation of the action to the user

### Runner
- Executes the written code in a sandboxed environment
- Handles different OS environments (Mac, Linux, Windows)
- Streams command output to user in real-time
- Gracefully handles errors and exceptions

### Feature
- Implements a new feature based on user's specification
- Modifies existing project files while maintaining code structure and style
- Performs incremental testing to verify feature is working as expected

### Patcher
- Debugs and fixes issues based on user's description or error message
- Analyzes existing code to identify potential root causes
- Suggests and implements fix, with explanation of the changes made

### Reporter
- Generates a comprehensive report summarizing the project
- Includes high-level overview, technical design, setup instructions, API docs, etc.
- Formats report in a clean, readable structure with table of contents
- Exports report as a PDF document

### Decision
- Handles special command-like instructions that don't fit other agents
- Maps commands to specific functions (git clone, browser interaction, etc.)
- Executes the corresponding function with provided arguments

Each agent follows a common pattern:
1. Prepare a prompt by rendering the Jinja2 template with current context
2. Query the LLM to get a response based on the prompt
3. Validate and parse the LLM's response to extract structured output
4. Perform any additional processing or side-effects (e.g., save to disk)
5. Return the result to the Agent Core for further action

Agents aim to be stateless and idempotent where possible. State and history is managed by the Agent Core and passed into the agents as needed. This allows for a modular, composable design.

## Language Models

Devika's natural language processing capabilities are driven by state-of-the-art LLMs. The `LLM` class provides a unified interface to interact with different language models:

- **Claude** (Anthropic): Claude models like claude-v1.3, claude-instant-v1.0, etc.
- **GPT-4/GPT-3** (OpenAI): Models like gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo, etc.
- **Self-hosted models** (via [Ollama](https://ollama.com/)): Allows using open-source models in a self-hosted environment

The `LLM` class abstracts out the specifics of each provider's API, allowing agents to interact with the models in a consistent way. It supports:
- Listing available models
- Generating completions based on a prompt
- Tracking and accumulating token usage over time

Choosing the right model for a given use case depends on factors like desired quality, speed, cost, etc. The modular design allows swapping out models easily.

## Browser Interaction

Devika can interact with webpages in an automated fashion to gather information and perform actions. This is powered by the `Browser` and `Crawler` classes.

The `Browser` class uses Playwright to provide high-level web automation primitives:
- Spawning a browser instance (Chromium)
- Navigating to a URL
- Querying DOM elements
- Extracting page content as text, Markdown, PDF, etc.
- Taking a screenshot of the page

The `Crawler` class defines an agent that can interact with a webpage based on natural language instructions. It leverages:
- Pre-defined browser actions like scroll, click, type, etc.
- A prompt template that provides examples of how to use these actions
- LLM to determine the best action to take based on current page content and objective

The `start_interaction` function sets up a loop where:
1. The current page content and objective is passed to the LLM
2. The LLM returns the next best action to take (e.g., "CLICK 12" or "TYPE 7 machine learning")
3. The Crawler executes this action on the live page
4. The process repeats from the updated page state

This allows performing a sequence of actions to achieve a higher-level objective (e.g., research a topic, fill out a form, interact with an app, etc.)

## Project Management

The `ProjectManager` class is responsible for creating, updating and querying projects and their associated metadata. Key functions include:

- Creating a new project and initializing its directory structure
- Deleting a project and its associated files
- Adding a message to a project's conversation history
- Retrieving messages for a given project
- Getting the latest user/AI message in a conversation
- Listing all projects
- Zipping a project's files for export

Project metadata is persisted in a SQLite database using SQLModel. The `Projects` table stores:
- Project name
- JSON-serialized conversation history

This allows the agent to work on multiple projects simultaneously and retain conversation history across sessions.

## Agent State Management

As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user.

## Agent State Management

As the AI agent works on a task, we need to track and display its internal state to the user. The `AgentState` class handles this by providing an interface to:

- Initialize a new agent state
- Add a state to the current sequence of states for a project
- Update the latest state for a project
- Query the latest state or entire state history for a project
- Mark the agent as active/inactive or task as completed

Agent state includes information like:
- Current step or action being executed
- Internal monologue reflecting the agent's current "thoughts"
- Browser interactions (URL visited, screenshot)
- Terminal interactions (command executed, output)
- Token usage so far

Like projects, agent states are also persisted in the SQLite DB using SQLModel. The `AgentStateModel` table stores:
- Project name
- JSON-serialized list of states

Having a persistent log of agent states is useful for:
- Providing real-time visibility to the user
- Auditing and debugging agent behavior
- Resuming from interruptions or failures

## Services

Devika integrates with external services to augment its capabilities:

- **GitHub**: Performing git operations like clone/pull, listing repos/commits/files, etc.
- **Netlify**: Deploying web apps and sites seamlessly

The `GitHub` and `Netlify` classes provide lightweight wrappers around the respective service APIs. They handle authentication, making HTTP requests, and parsing responses.

This allows Devika to perform actions like:
- Cloning a repo given a GitHub URL
- Listing a user's GitHub repos
- Creating a new Netlify site
- Deploying a directory to Netlify
- Providing the deployed site URL to the user

Integrations are done in a modular way so that new services can be added easily.

## Utilities

Devika makes use of several utility modules to support its functioning:

- `Config`: Loads and provides access to configuration settings (API keys, folder paths, etc.)
- `Logger`: Sets up logging to console and file, with support for log levels and colors
- `ReadCode`: Recursively reads code files in a directory and converts them into a Markdown format
- `SentenceBERT`: Extracts keywords and semantic information from text using SentenceBERT embeddings
- `Experts`: A collection of domain-specific knowledge bases to assist in certain areas (e.g., webdev, physics, chemistry, math)

The utility modules aim to provide reusable functionality that is used across different parts of the system.

## Gamification Engine

To enhance user engagement, Devika incorporates a gamification engine that includes:

- **Points System**: Users earn points for completing tasks, answering questions correctly, and following instructions.
- **Badges and Achievements**: Users receive badges for reaching milestones, such as completing a certain number of tasks or achieving a high score.
- **Leaderboard**: Displays top users based on points earned, encouraging friendly competition.
- **Challenges and Mini-Games**: Provides additional opportunities for users to earn points and badges through interactive challenges and mini-games.

The gamification engine is designed to make interactions with Devika more engaging and rewarding, motivating users to learn and complete tasks effectively.

## Predictive Assistance Module

Devika leverages machine learning models to provide predictive assistance, which includes:

- **Predictive Text**: Suggests the next steps or inputs based on user patterns and historical data.
- **Smart Defaults**: Automatically fills in common or likely values to minimize user input.
- **Adaptive Learning**: Continuously learns from user interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of predictions and suggestions.

The predictive assistance module helps streamline user interactions, making the system more intuitive and efficient.

## Interactive Guidance

To help users navigate and understand the system, Devika provides:

- **Guided Tours**: Interactive tutorials that guide users through common tasks and features.
- **Tooltips**: Contextual tips that provide additional information and guidance when users hover over certain elements.
- **Real-Time Feedback**: Immediate feedback and confirmation messages to ensure users are on the right track.

Interactive guidance ensures that users, regardless of their technical expertise, can effectively use Devika and achieve their goals.

## Conclusion

Devika is a complex system that combines multiple AI and automation techniques to deliver an intelligent programming assistant. Key design principles include:

- **Modularity**: Breaking down functionality into specialized agents and services
- **Flexibility**: Supporting different LLMs, services, and domains in a pluggable fashion
- **Persistence**: Storing project and agent state in a DB to enable pause/resume and auditing
- **Transparency**: Surfacing agent thought process and interactions to user in real-time
- **Engagement**: Incorporating gamification elements to make interactions rewarding and motivating

By understanding how the different components work together, we can extend, optimize, and scale Devika to take on increasingly sophisticated software engineering tasks. The agent-based architecture provides a strong foundation to build more advanced AI capabilities in the future.
